Jared / team  thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our demo and suggested next steps so we stay aligned: 

Summary from today
- Showed Redwood Dedicated performance for your gen-2 LLM (approx 30 req/s at 2s p95 on p4-like nodes) and fallbacks to smaller variants for burst handling.
- Discussed capacity guarantees (reserved pools + burst) vs hyperscaler committed instances.
- Covered security posture (VPC, KMS, SOC2 artifacts).

Open items / asks from Acme
- Can you confirm expected sustained qps and burst patterns (sample hours/days)?
- Procurement: preferred contract term (monthly vs 12/24mo) and required SLAs.
- Any compliance evidence besides SOC2 we should prep?

Proposed next technical tests
1) Side-by-side run: Redwood Dedicated reserved pool vs your hyperscaler committed instances using your workload (50k sample tokens/day). Goal: compare p95 latency, cost/TU, and cold-start behavior.
2) Stress window test: 30 minute burst to validate autoscaling and burst capacity.
3) Failover exercise: route to a lower-cost variant for graceful degradation.

I've attached a short comparison doc (high-level numbers & test plan) and an MAPP spreadsheet to collect configuration parameters. If you can populate the MAPP (Acme_MAPP.xlsx) with qps/latency targets and expected growth, we'll schedule the run.

Attachments:

Proposed timing: run tests next week (Dec 79). If that works, I'll book a 90-minute window and loop in our infra engineer.

Jared  good questions, answered inline below. Quick call tomorrow if helpful.

Q1: Capacity guarantees
- Redwood Dedicated offers reserved GPU pools backed by an SLA: reserved nodes are dedicated to the customer and are not preemptible. You get guaranteed throughput for the committed pool. Burst capacity is a separate add-on (burst pool) that can be configured to kick in automatically; that pool is subject to availability but we offer contractual burst obligations in enterprise contracts.

Q2: Oversubscription / rapid scaling
- If you exceed reserved capacity, options are: (a) auto-burst to burst pool (policy-controlled), (b) route to a compatible model variant (smaller/quantized) to preserve latency, or (c) temporary run on hyperscaler partners (we can pre-arrange partner capacity for critical events). We also provide pre-warm options for scheduled heavy windows.

SLA notes
- Standard Dedicated SLA: 99.9% uptime for the control plane + per-node availability guarantees for reserved pools. We can discuss 99.95% for multi-region runs.

Pricing bands
- I attached the high-level bands in the comparison doc. 12mo vs 24mo discounts are listed; deeper committed discounts are possible with a footprint commit.

Proposed test plan (concrete)
- Dec 8: baseline run (10:0011:30 PT)  compare latency/cost on Redwood Dedicated reserved vs your hyperscaler committed instances using a 5k-sample workload.
- Dec 9: burst test (13:0013:45 PT)  30 minute stress window.

Please confirm the two windows or suggest alternatives. I'll invite Marissa (our PM for Dedicated) and our infra lead.

Thanks 
Markus
